title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the preceding pages). X is a 'carte triangulée positive' of type {0,1,∞}: a set R of triangles (flags) with involutions τ_0, τ_1, τ_∞. τ_i is reflection across the side of type i, the side opposite the vertex of type i. 'Positive' means the surface is oriented, so R = R^+ ⊔ R^- and each τ_i reverses orientation. The rotations are ρ_i = τ_j τ_k for {i,j,k} = {0,1,∞}, so ρ_1 = τ_0 τ_∞. The order of ρ_i at a vertex is half the number of triangles around it; Grothendieck calls this the 'ordre réduit', as opposed to the 'ordre ordinaire'.

The space is X̃^{**}, the real oriented blow-up of the surface at all vertices. Each vertex φ is replaced by a boundary circle.
- R_r^{ij} is the point on the circle over the vertex of type i of r, in the direction of the side ij.
- λ_r^i is the arc of that circle inside the sector of r, from R_r^{i,i+1} to R_r^{i,i-1}.
- a_r^k is the arc along the side of type k, joining the two circles at its ends.
- Relations (10) and (12) (the triangle loop b^∞ b^1 b^0 = 1) give a presentation of the fundamental groupoid π_1(X̃^{**}, {R_r^{ij}}).

This page makes three points.

(1) The formalism makes sense for every positive triangulated map of type {0,1,∞}, not only for the barycentric subdivision of an ordinary map X. The barycentric case is characterised by the second relation (τ_0τ_∞)^2 = 1, i.e. ρ_1^2 = 1. This says vertices of type 1 (edge midpoints) have reduced order 2, i.e. 4 triangles around them, and equivalently that τ_0 and τ_∞ commute. In general, i.e. for hypermaps, ρ_1 plays no special role relative to ρ_0 and ρ_∞: it is the one-notch rotation of r about its type-1 vertex, in the sense given by the orientation of r.

(2) Definition (13) introduces two 'double-notch' rotations about the type-i vertex. Composition is written right to left.
- Λ_r^i = (λ^i_{τ_{i+1}(r)})^{-1} λ^i_r. It runs along λ^i_r to the side {i,i-1}, crosses into the oppositely oriented neighbour τ_{i+1}(r), and runs back along that triangle's λ^i, arriving at its point R^{i,i+1}.
- Λ'^i_r = λ^i_{τ_{i-1}(r)} (λ^i_r)^{-1}. It runs from R_r^{i,i-1} back to R_r^{i,i+1}, crosses the side {i,i+1} into τ_{i-1}(r), and ends at R^{i,i-1}_{τ_{i-1}(r)}.
- Both rotate in the sense fixed by the orientation of r, resp. the opposite sense.

(3) Relations (14) Λ^i_r Λ^i_{τ(r)} = 1 and Λ'^i_r Λ'^i_{τ(r)} = 1. Here τ(r) is the adjacent triangle where Λ (resp. Λ') ends. Doing the double notch from there, with the reversed orientation, retraces the path backwards. These are therefore 'redundancy' relations, as the next page calls them: they make Λ for negatively oriented triangles the inverse of Λ for positive ones. They do not say that a vertex has order 2.

Purpose. The next page fixes the index 1 and eliminates the points R^{0∞}, R^{∞0} and the arcs a^1. It obtains a smaller presentation with generators λ^1, Λ^0, Λ^∞, a^0, a^∞ and one relation (16) per positive triangle. This is a combinatorial presentation of the fundamental groupoid of the punctured surface attached to a dessin/hypermap, which is the groundwork for describing the Galois action on Teichmüller groupoids combinatorially.
errors: Index slip in (13)/(14) for the unprimed Λ, as transcribed: the target and the partner in (14) are written with τ_{i-1}(r). On the geometric reading (the path crosses the side {i,i-1}, of type i+1), the endpoint should be R^{i,i+1}_{τ_{i+1}(r)} and (14) should read Λ^i_r Λ^i_{τ_{i+1}(r)} = 1. The primed version with τ_{i-1} is consistent. This may be a reading problem, or a slip in Grothendieck's own index conventions.

Minor wording point, not an error: ρ_1^2 = 1 characterises triangulations that are barycentric subdivisions of a map only together with the type-{0,1,∞} colouring. Grothendieck implicitly assumes this.

ideas.what: General triangulated maps of type {0,1,∞} (hypermaps) versus barycentric subdivisions of maps, characterised by (τ_0τ_∞)^2 = 1, i.e. type-1 vertices of valence 4
ideas.modern_name: Hypermaps vs maps; the cartographic group C_2 with the extra relation (σ_0σ_2)^2 = 1
ideas.usually_credited_to: Cori (1975), Walsh (1975), Jones–Singerman (1978); Grothendieck (Esquisse d'un programme, 1984)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (cartographic groups, maps vs general triangulations)

ideas.what: One-notch rotations ρ_i = τ_jτ_k about vertices; reduced vs ordinary order (half the number of incident triangles)
ideas.modern_name: Rotation generators of the oriented cartographic group / monodromy of a dessin

ideas.what: Double-notch boundary arcs Λ, Λ' around blown-up vertices, used to present the fundamental groupoid of the punctured surface with base points on the boundary circles
ideas.modern_name: Combinatorial presentation of π_1-groupoid of a surface from a triangulation/ribbon graph (oriented real blow-up)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; related to ribbon-graph presentations (Penner, Kontsevich) and to Grothendieck–Teichmüller groupoid work (Drinfeld, Ihara, Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses Teichmüller groupoids with tangential base points, but not this explicit presentation

deep.surprise_reason: Bookkeeping page in a combinatorial presentation of a fundamental groupoid. The map/hypermap distinction is standard and appears in the Esquisse; the Λ relations are trivial redundancy relations. Nothing here is absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: In (13), what is transcribed as 'λ^{i-1}_{τ_{i+1}(r)}' should probably be read as (λ^i_{τ_{i+1}(r)})^{-1}. The '-1' is an inverse exponent, not the index i-1, as the parentheses and the geometry indicate.
In (14), the first box likely reads Λ^i_r Λ^i_{τ_{i+1}(r)} = 1, with τ_{i+1} rather than τ_{i-1}; the second box has τ_{i-1}.
Line 3: 'sans que celle-ci soit nécessairement [barycentrique]' — the struck word is likely an earlier attempt at the same phrase; the sense is 'not necessarily a barycentric subdivision'.
'qui s'énonce donc par la suite' is more likely 'qui s'abandonne donc par la suite' or similar: the relation is dropped in what follows.
